office_does: The three county commissioners set and oversee the county budget, adopt ordinances for unincorporated areas, oversee roads and public works, and sit on regional boards.
race_blurb: Open seat: Commissioner Cindy Carter is retiring after 20 years. District 3 voters nominated rancher and bookkeeper Kelly Raap and Quincy School Board director Shannon Durfee, both preferring the Republican Party, and all county voters choose between them in November. Both stress fiscal responsibility, infrastructure and planning for growth.

candidates.summary: Rural Ephrata ranch co-owner and bookkeeper making her first run for office, who led the District 3 primary.
highlights: 'Just because you have money in the bank does not mean it has to be spent' [S6]
Pledges to protect the rural economy and support farmers, ranchers and businesses [S1]
Supports investing in public safety, roads and infrastructure [S4]

experience.basis: First-time candidate for any elected office who runs on farm and bookkeeping experience and 'decisions based on facts, not politics'.

spending.basis: Repeated restraint language (balance a budget without wasting resources; money in the bank need not be spent), tempered by support for infrastructure investment.

candidates.summary: Quincy School Board director, Quincy Rotary president, small-business owner and hospital-foundation director running on practical leadership and responsible growth.
highlights: Wants growth to benefit current residents 'not just outside interests' through responsible planning [S4]
Pledges fiscal responsibility, infrastructure, transparency and local voices in county decisions [S1]
Former Washington State Patrol communications officer for 10 years [S2]

experience.basis: Holds one local elected office (school board) and presents her background as community leadership rather than career politics.
